mcqs.learning_point: Recognise differences in food, dress and customs
mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly contrasts the traditional food, dress and customs of the people of Punjab with those of the people of Kerala?

options.A: Punjab: rice and fish; white dhoti; Onam festival. Kerala: wheat roti; turban; Baisakhi celebration.
options.B: Punjab: wheat roti and sarson da saag; bright phulkari dupatta; Baisakhi festival. Kerala: rice and coconut-based dishes; mundu and kasavu; Onam festival.
options.C: Punjab: millet porridge; simple cotton shirt; Pongal festival. Kerala: barley bread; heavy woolen coat; Diwali fireworks.
options.D: Punjab: tea and biscuits; kurta-pajama; Holi colors. Kerala: coffee and cake; jeans; Christmas tree.

mcqs.answer: Punjab: wheat roti and sarson da saag; bright phulkari dupatta; Baisakhi festival. Kerala: rice and coconut-based dishes; mundu and kasavu; Onam festival.
mcqs.explanation: Option B accurately describes the typical food (wheat roti and sarson da saag in Punjab; rice and coconut dishes in Kerala), traditional dress (phulkari dupatta in Punjab; mundu and kasavu in Kerala) and major festivals (Baisakhi in Punjab; Onam in Kerala). The other options mix up regional attributes, pairing foods, clothing or festivals with the wrong state.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand diversity as a feature of society
mcqs.question: Which statement best explains why diversity is considered a fundamental feature of Indian society?

options.A: Because every Indian follows the same language, religion and cultural practices.
options.B: Because India has multiple languages, religions, cuisines, clothing styles and regional customs that coexist.
options.C: Because the Indian Constitution mandates a single national culture for all citizens.
options.D: Because only a few states in India have distinct cultural traits while the rest are homogeneous.

mcqs.answer: Because India has multiple languages, religions, cuisines, clothing styles and regional customs that coexist.
mcqs.explanation: Option B captures the essence of diversity: the coexistence of many languages, religions, foods, dress and customs across different regions. Options A, C and D are incorrect as they deny or ignore the pluralistic nature of Indian society, which is contrary to the constitutional recognition of diversity.

mcqs.question: Which of the following illustrates linguistic diversity in India?

options.A: All people in India speak Hindi only.
options.B: People in different states speak languages such as Tamil, Bengali, Marathi, and Assamese.
options.C: Every Indian uses English as the sole medium of communication.
options.D: Only one language is taught in all Indian schools.

mcqs.answer: People in different states speak languages such as Tamil, Bengali, Marathi, and Assamese.
mcqs.explanation: Option B correctly shows that various regions use different mother tongues, reflecting linguistic diversity. Options A, C, and D incorrectly suggest a single language for the whole country, which is not true.

mcqs.question: Which example best demonstrates regional diversity in India?

options.A: All Indian states celebrate the same festival on the same day.
options.B: The climate, food habits and traditional houses differ between the desert region of Rajasthan and the coastal region of Kerala.
options.C: Every state follows identical agricultural practices.
options.D: All regions use the same style of clothing throughout the country.

mcqs.answer: The climate, food habits and traditional houses differ between the desert region of Rajasthan and the coastal region of Kerala.
mcqs.explanation: Option B highlights differences in climate, cuisine and architecture between two distinct regions, which is the essence of regional diversity. The other options incorrectly suggest uniformity across regions.

mcqs.question: Cultural diversity refers to:

options.A: The presence of many different cultural practices, beliefs, arts and traditions within a society.
options.B: The existence of a single, uniform culture across the entire nation.
options.C: Only the variety of languages spoken in a country.
options.D: The number of schools in a region.

mcqs.answer: The presence of many different cultural practices, beliefs, arts and traditions within a society.
mcqs.explanation: Option A correctly defines cultural diversity as the coexistence of varied cultural elements. Options B, C, and D either deny diversity or limit it to language or education, which are not comprehensive definitions.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise differences in food, dress and customs
mcqs.question: A school is organizing a cultural day where students will showcase food, dress and customs from different Indian states. Which of the following actions best respects the principle of recognising these differences?

options.A: Ask every student to wear the same uniform and serve only one type of food to avoid confusion.
options.B: Allow each class to present a dish, traditional attire and a short performance that represent their own state’s unique customs.
options.C: Select only the most popular state’s culture to represent the whole country.
options.D: Prohibit any discussion of customs to keep the event neutral.

mcqs.answer: Allow each class to present a dish, traditional attire and a short performance that represent their own state’s unique customs.
mcqs.explanation: Option B actively showcases the distinct food, dress and customs of various states, aligning with the goal of recognising diversity. Options A, C, and D suppress or ignore the differences, which defeats the purpose of the activity.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand diversity as a feature of society
mcqs.question: Which of the following scenarios best illustrates diversity as a feature of Indian society?

options.A: A village where every household follows the same religion, speaks the same language and eats the same food.
options.B: A city where people celebrate Diwali, Eid, Christmas and Pongal; speak Hindi, Tamil, Urdu and English; and enjoy a variety of regional cuisines.
options.C: A school that teaches only one textbook for all subjects.
options.D: A state that bans all foreign cultural influences.

mcqs.answer: A city where people celebrate Diwali, Eid, Christmas and Pongal; speak Hindi, Tamil, Urdu and English; and enjoy a variety of regional cuisines.
mcqs.explanation: Option B reflects multiple religions, languages and foods coexisting in one society, which is a clear example of diversity. Options A, C, and D describe uniformity or restriction, not diversity.

mcqs.question: Ravi, a student from Karnataka, moves to a school in West Bengal. He notices his classmates speak Bengali, Hindi, and English. Which observation best shows linguistic diversity in his new environment?

options.A: All students speak only Bengali at home and in school.
options.B: Students use different languages—Bengali, Hindi, and English—depending on the context.
options.C: The school has banned the use of any language other than English.
options.D: Every student is required to learn Sanskrit as the sole second language.

mcqs.answer: Students use different languages—Bengali, Hindi, and English—depending on the context.
mcqs.explanation: Option B captures the presence of multiple languages being used, which is the hallmark of linguistic diversity. Options A, C, and D describe monolingual or restricted language use, which does not illustrate diversity.
